Outcome: nothing in slot 1 qualifies for a follow-up. Only stage A was played, and only in part; stages B (40 usual) and C (80 fresh) were not played for any variant.

What went wrong: the slot ran at about 4.3 worlds a minute, not the planned 45. Sweep w1a (19 variants x 16 usual worlds = 304 worlds) started at about 10:55:30 UTC and was stopped by the 11:21:00 cut with 111 worlds played. Each of the 4 keys plays 8 worlds at a time (2 variants x its 4 seeds) and a batch took about 5 minutes. Because a slot holds one sweep at a time and nothing may be killed, the slot stayed locked on w1a past 11:14, so no second sweep could start.

Not played at all (11 of 19 variants, they sat later in the file): w1-p2h19s24 (rampPow 2, feeHold 19, feeSteps 24); the whole late ramp set w1-ls105e90 (lateStart 1.05, lateEvery 90), w1-ls100e90 (lateStart 1.0, lateEvery 90), w1-ls105e180s07 (lateStart 1.05, lateEvery 180, lateStep 0.07), w1-ls095e80s13 (lateStart 0.95, lateEvery 80, lateStep 0.13), w1-ls125e180s07 (lateStart 1.25, lateEvery 180, lateStep 0.07); the whole urgent ramp set w1-us14p30 (urgentStart 1.4, urgentStep 0.3), w1-us12e15p30 (urgentStart 1.2, urgentEvery 15, urgentStep 0.3), w1-us18e25p20 (urgentStart 1.8, urgentEvery 25, urgentStep 0.2); and the cross moves w1-ls105us14 (lateStart 1.05, urgentStart 1.4), w1-ls100e90us14p30 (lateStart 1.0, lateEvery 90, urgentStart 1.4, urgentStep 0.3). The late and urgent ramps, where the only positive singles were (lateStart down +96, urgentStart down +22), are therefore still untested as joint moves. The changes file is ready to replay as it stands: C:\Users\trevo\spread\data\scan\w1a.json (sweep file C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\sweeps\w1a.json; a replay needs a new sweep name).

What the runs showed (normal ramp only, 16 usual worlds, se 120 to 220, so each line alone is weak):
- All six finished joint moves of feeCap / feeHold / rampLead / rampPow are behind the base (base on these 16 worlds: mean 17720, on-time 97.3, lowest 93.4).
- No compensation between cap and hold or cap and lead: lower cap with longer hold -85 (t -0.7), lower cap with later cap arrival -186 (t -1.1), higher cap with shorter hold -250 (t -1.6), higher cap reached earlier -430 (t -2.4, the clearest result; lowest on-time 93.0, 0.4 under the base). Raising the cap looks worse than lowering it in both pairs, in line with the singles (feeCap up -158, down -177).
- No compensation between power and lead either: rampPow 2 with rampLead 240 -160 (t -1.1), rampPow 1.1 with rampLead 160 -75 (t -0.3, se 224, worst world -2678).
- The cap with power pair was cut: feeCap 1.3 + rampPow 1.1 is -4 on 9 worlds, feeCap 1.5 + rampPow 2 is +105 on 6 worlds (se 314). Neither set of worlds includes m7 or m11, the two worlds with the lowest on-time share, so their on-time floors (96.0, 96.9) are not comparable with the base's 93.4.
- Read as a whole this agrees with the single-knob search: cand5 sits at a local optimum for the normal ramp, and these two-knob moves did not find a ridge.

WHAT WENT WRONG: the slot was about ten times slower than the planned 45 worlds a minute. Sweep w2a (18 variants x 16 usual worlds = 288 worlds) started at 10:54:58 UTC; sweep.ts plays the variants in file order, 8 worlds at a time on each of the 4 keys, so results arrive two variants (32 worlds) a batch, and the batches ended at about 11:05 or earlier, 11:09:27, 11:15:38, with the fourth cut at 11:21:00. Only 6 variants reached 16 worlds and 2 more reached 12 and 11; the other 10 were never played. Stage B (24 other usual worlds), stage C (80 fresh worlds) and a second stage A were NOT played: the slot was locked by w2a until the cut and I was not allowed to stop it. Every number above is 16-world (or fewer) stage A data with se 100-330, so nothing is established.

NOT PLAYED (in bot/sweeps/w2a.json, zero results): w2-fk1175-lpo27 (feeK 1.175, lambdaPerOpen 27), w2-lpo27-lfo20 (lambdaPerOpen 27, lambdaFreeOpen 20), w2-lpo21-lfo10 (lambdaPerOpen 21, lambdaFreeOpen 10), w2-calm (shockSd 0.02, placeShockSd 0.01, daySd 0.02), w2-lively (shockSd 0.04, placeShockSd 0.03, daySd 0.04), w2-ev-strong (war -0.263, outage 0.302), w2-ev-weak (war -0.183, outage 0.222), w2-tr-up (trustGain 0.0156, trustValue 1.2), w2-tr-dn (trustGain 0.0092, trustValue 0.8), w2-lpo27-war183-sc065 (lambdaPerOpen 27, war -0.183, scale 0.065). So the calmer/livelier model, war with outage, and the trust pair were not tested at all; because of the file order only the scale group and two feeK-with-lambdaPerOpen variants ran.

WHAT THE RUNS SHOWED (all weak evidence, 16 worlds):
- Narrower scale with lower feeK does not look like a gain: scale 0.06 + feeK 1.125 -28 (t -0.1), scale 0.065 + feeK 1.125 +128 (t +0.5) with the m11 on-time down to 92.6, scale 0.06 + feeK 1.10 -397 (t -1.2, worst world -4538, min margin 9849). Lower feeK wins more orders (won 444.2 / 439.2 / 456.7 against the base's 423.7) but average on-time drops (97.0 / 97.3 / 96.9 against 97.3) and the margin does not follow; feeK 1.10 is too low even with the narrow scale.
- Scale with priorLevel: no direction helps. scale 0.06 + priorLevel 1.57 -53 (t -0.2), scale 0.06 + priorLevel 1.51 -116 (t -0.6, lowest on-time 92.9, 1 world under 93), scale 0.08 + priorLevel 1.57 -158 (t -1.2; fewer wins 411.3, on-time 97.6, floor 95.3). The wider scale with the higher prior is a safer but poorer bot; the narrow scale with the lower prior wins more and lowers the on-time floor. No sign of a scale x priorLevel interaction beyond the sum of the two negative singles.
- feeK with lambdaPerOpen (cut, 11-12 worlds): feeK 1.125 + lambdaPerOpen 45 +222 (t +1.2 on 11, worst -505, on-time 98.0) against feeK 1.125 + lambdaPerOpen 27 +47 (t +0.5 on 12). This hints that a lower base price pairs with MORE backlog pressure, not less (the opposite pairing of the lambdaPerOpen 27 single), and with a small downside; it is the one joint move here that deserves a re-run on the 40 usual and the fresh worlds. Caution: these two have different world subsets from the others (the base mean on their worlds is lower), and their lowest on-time values are not comparable with the 16-world base floor.
- On-time floor: every variant stayed ranked in every world played (all above 90%); the lowest single world was 92.6 (w2-sc065-fk1125, m11).

So the startFallback-with-costStart pairs and the whole costSameDay/costPrivate/costNote group are untested. costNote was in no variant.

WHAT THE RUNS SHOWED (all on 16 usual worlds, se 129 to 228, so every statement here is inside noise):
- Monday/Thursday day fallbacks: the analysis direction (Mon 1.12, Thu 1.28) was -193 (t -0.8); the reverse (Mon 1.28, Thu 1.12) was +145 (t +1.1, 11/16 up). The sign flips with the direction, which is the one consistent pattern, but the reverse also had the lowest on-time of the set: 92.9 on m11, one world under 93, against the base's 93.4.
- startModel.lnOLane -0.855 on top of the Mon/Thu move: -193 became -89. Adding costStartMean 0.97 as well: +22. lnOLane with costStartMean 0.97 and no day move: +41. The costStartMean 0.97 variants won more orders (won 431.7 and 434.9 against the base's 423.7), consistent with a lower quote level; w3-mt-ln-m97 had mean on-time 97.0 against 97.3.
- Band: wider (0.55..1.0) -115 (t -0.6). Narrower (0.65..0.91) -257 on 10 worlds and shifted up (0.65..1.0) -69 on 8 worlds are partial and not comparable with the 16-world rows: the worlds that finished exclude m7 and m11, the two lowest on-time worlds, so their on-time floors (96.7, 96.5) say nothing.

FROM READING bot/desk.ts startPlan (lines 1286-1307), not from a test: the expected fee that feeds the quote cost is chance x start + (1 - chance) x startFallback, using the plain startFallback, not the day's value. Two consequences: (1) since cand5 sets startFallbackDay for all five weekdays, the plain startFallback acts mainly as a quote-cost knob, raising cost by about (1 - chance) x the change; (2) a day fallback equal to startFallback makes the opening fee the minimiser of that expected fee, so small day-fallback moves change the price level only at second order and need no costStartMean pairing, while lnOLane and startFallback move it at first order.

reports.notes:
RESULT: nothing in this theme meets the follow-up rule. 31 variants played in four sweeps (w4a 18x16 usual, w4b 8x24 t-worlds, w4c 1x80 fresh, w4d 9x40 usual); all four sweeps finished, the last at 11:14:48 UTC. All numbers are as cmp.py printed them (tn1-base for usual, tn1-base-u for fresh).

WHAT THE RUNS SHOWED
- minAwake down (180/200) with a stricter guard (lateTarget 0.025, ctrlPow 4) is clearly bad: -588 and -501 on 16 worlds (t -2.0, -2.2), floor 92.4. Orders won rise from 423.7 to about 442, so the extra tight orders lose money; the stricter guard does not rescue it. Adding buf20/sl120 on top (-458) or using lateShadow 7000 as the guard (-346) does not help either.
- minAwake 300 with a looser guard (lateTarget 0.035, ctrlPow 2): +56 on 16, then -264 on the 24 t worlds; -136 (t -1.2) over 40. minAwake 240 looks like the optimum in both directions.
- Lowering the cost of lateness (lateShadow 5000, alone or with lateLoss 0.3 or lateTarget 0.025) wins more orders (432 to 445 against 428.8) and loses margin: sh5-lt25 -216 (t -2.0), sh5-ll3-lt25-p4 -434 (t -2.8), buf20-sl120-sh5-lt25 -201 (t -1.5). Raising it also loses: sh7-ll5 -303 (t -2.8 on 16), sh7-ll3 -234, sh8-lt35 -114 over 40. The lateShadow/lateLoss/lateTarget block is at a local optimum; no joint direction helped.
- lateTarget and ctrlPow moved in opposite senses: lt35-p4 is flat on margin (-5) but drops the floor to 92.3 (m11); lt25-p2 is -122 (t -1.3). No gain from trading the two.
- Drops: dropSafe 240 with dropBump 1.05 was +96 on 16 and -31 over 40; with dropBump 1.15 -271 on 16; dropSafe 180 with dropBump 1.0 -125 on 16, floor 92.9. The suggested dropSafe 240 gives nothing measurable, and adding it to other moves (buf20-sl120-ds240 -23, the two -ds240-db105 combinations -306 and -144 on t worlds) did not help.
- deliveryBuffer with minSlack is the only region with non-negative results: buf20-sl120 +28, buf20-sl90 +103 (t +1.1), both with floor 94.2 on the 40 usual. But the step further (buf10-sl90) was -147 on 16, the opposite direction (buf40-sl180) -192 on 16, and buf20-sl120 on the 80 fresh worlds was -63 (t -0.8) with floor 92.5 against 93.4. So the usual-world floor gain (it comes from m7 and m11) does not generalise.
- Stacking positives did not add up: every combination of two stage-A winners was worse than its parts (buf20-sl120-sh7 +167 on 16 became -8 over 40; buf20-sl120-sh8-lt35 -219, buf20-sl120-sh7-ds240-db105 -306 on the t worlds).
- 16-world screening was unreliable here: all five stage-A leaders (+56 to +167 on 16) were negative on the 24 t worlds (-3 to -264). saveShare was not tested (zero effect as a single).

DEVIATIONS FROM THE PLAN
- w4b carried three new combined tags besides the five stage-A leaders; those three were played on t1-t24 only (never on the s/m worlds), so their n is 24.
- No variant reached t of 1 over 40 after stage B. Stage C was still played for w4-buf20-sl120 alone, because it showed a higher floor at equal margin (the theme's second goal); it failed on fresh.
- The second round (w4d) skipped the 16-world screen and played 9 new variants directly on all 40 usual worlds.

CUT BY THE DEADLINE
- w4-buf20-sl90, the best variant over 40, came out of the last sweep (ended 11:14:48, after the 11:14:00 start limit), so it has no fresh run.
- The 13 variants dropped after stage A have 16 worlds only.

Changes files: C:\Users\trevo\spread\data\scan\w5a.json, w5b.json, w5c.json, w5d.json; sweep files C:\Users\trevo\spread\bot\sweeps\w5a.json to w5d.json. Numbers are as cmp.py printed them (usual against tn1-base, fresh against tn1-base-u).

FLOOR. By the stated rule (lowest on-time not under the base's by more than half a point) no variant passes on the fresh worlds: base-u lowest is 93.4 (h65; h24 is 93.9), and every variant played on fresh has its lowest world between 90.7 and 92.8, on h24 in six of seven cases (h65 for pp110-top5). Even top2/top3 without any switch drop h24 to 92.8, so part of the h24 drop comes from lateStart 1.05 + lambdaPerOpen 27 themselves, not only from private pickups. On the 40 usual worlds the floors were at or above the base's (93.3 to 94.7 against 93.4), except tr-pp 92.8. All variants were ranked in all worlds (lowest seen 90.7).

INTERACTIONS.
- lateStart 1.05 + lambdaPerOpen 27 add up roughly as the singles suggested (+96 and +109 alone; +184 together on 40 usual, t 2.0), but only +94 (t 1.3) on fresh. With minSlack 120 added: +164 usual, +144 fresh (t 2.1 both).
- The weaker singles do not stack on 16 worlds: top5 (adds deliveryBuffer 20, market.war -0.263) -8, top7 (adds lateStep 0.07, urgentStart 1.4) +35 with floor 92.9, top5 with war up instead +143 (se 251). Larger steps (0.95 / 21 / 90) +66 against +213 for top3 on the same 16 worlds: no sign that bigger moves help. All within noise at n 16.
- Private pickups give the larger fresh gain: all five fresh variants with quotePrivatePickup are +231 to +347 (t 2.1 to 3.8), against +94 / +144 for top2 / top3. They also cost floor on fresh (90.7 to 92.7).
- Offer model: alone it was negative elsewhere (p1-om -123, t -1.1, 40 worlds), and with top2 only it is flat (om-top2 +28, om3-top2 with offerMin 0.003 +70, n 16), but together with private pickups it is positive (om-pp +175 t 1.4 usual, +231 t 2.1 fresh) and om-pp110-top2 has the best usual floor (94.7) and the best fresh t (3.8). offerMin 0.003 against 0.004 shows no visible difference at n 16.
- minAwake as a safety for private pickups did not work: minAwake 360 removes the gain (pp-aw +13, pp110-aw -240 on 16 worlds; orders won 415.6 / 418.0 against 423.7 for the base), and minAwake 300 in pp110-aw-top3 gave the worst fresh floor of all (90.7 on h24). Adding the offer model to that set (om-pp110-aw-top3, fresh only) had 92.4 on h24.
- Trade-ins: tr-pp +112 (t 0.9, 40 usual, floor 92.8 on m11, one world under 93); tr-om +75 on 16 worlds. No sign of an interaction worth more runs.
- Noise warning: on 16 worlds variants with private pickups have se 170 to 330 and are not separable from each other (pp110-top2 +21, pp110-top3 -41, but pp110-top5 +383, om-pp110-top2 +427); om-pp110-top2 fell from +427 (t 2.5) on 16 worlds to +205 (t 1.7) on 40. The single om-pp110 (-159) and pp110-aw (-240) results at n 16 contradict p1-priv-f110 (+210 on 40) and should not be read as evidence against privateFee 1.1.

CUT BY THE DEADLINE. 13 of the 20 stage A variants have only 16 usual worlds. w5-tr-pp was not played on fresh worlds. w5-om-pp110-aw-top3 was played on fresh worlds only (no usual-world numbers). No second stage A with new joint moves was run; the remaining time went to fresh-world runs of all six variants that were ahead with t of 1.4 or more on 40 usual worlds. Single switches were not run in this slot (p1-* read only: p1-priv +106 t 0.9, p1-priv-f110 +210 t 1.5 floor 92.7, p1-om -123 t -1.1, p1-om-min3 -73 on 31 worlds; trade-in p1 tags had no results when read at about 10:55 UTC).

Nothing went wrong: no ssh failures, no file outside bot/sweeps/w5*.json and data/scan/w5* was created or changed, only slot 5 was used.
